subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should OpenClaw expose granular Discord message permissions, and if so should the existing `actions.messages` boolean remain the compatibility shorthand for all message operations?
rationale: This is a new public configuration and least-privilege policy surface; the repository guidance treats added config/default behavior and permission changes as compatibility-sensitive product decisions.

options.title: Adopt a backward-compatible granular gate
options.body: Keep the boolean shorthand while adding a documented structured Discord-only gate for send, read, edit, and delete, with explicit fallback semantics.

options.title: Keep the coarse gate
options.body: Retain the current single permission if the maintenance cost and policy complexity outweigh the least-privilege benefit.

options.title: Choose separate named action gates
options.body: Add distinct top-level Discord action booleans instead of a nested object if maintainers prefer a flatter public configuration contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt a backward-compatible granular gate
recommendation.body: Keep the boolean shorthand while adding a documented structured Discord-only gate for send, read, edit, and delete, with explicit fallback semantics.
